I think about my land the same way I did last year. Thirteen mu is what my husband and I can handle ourselves, though we hire the combine when wheat and maize come off. My oldest works in town so it is just two of us in the field most days.

For wheat, I do what I always do. After the maize comes off in October, I have the tractor man run the rotary over the stubble, then I broadcast my base fertilizer and plant. I buy the compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, same as Old Zhang next door — one bag for every mu, that is 50 jin, no 100 jin, one bag is 80 jin I think, anyway one bag per mu. Then in spring when the wheat turns green I put urea, half a bag per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I add more, better too much than a thin harvest. I water four times — once before winter so it does not freeze dry, then green-up, jointing, and when the head comes out. The well is right there, the electric is cheap enough. I spray for the weeds once in spring and for the aphids when I see them on the heads, maybe twice.

For maize, after wheat I do not plow, I just have the seeder go straight in behind the wheat combine, saves time and saves the moisture. Hybrid seed of course, everyone buys hybrid now, the dealer in town has the same kind my neighbors plant. Base fertilizer one bag compound per mu with the seed, then when the maize is waist-high I put urea down the rows, almost a bag per mu. Maize eats a lot, if I short it the cobs come out small. Rain is usually enough in summer but if July is dry I water once or twice. One spray for the borer when I see the holes in the leaves.

My yields are like the neighbors' — wheat about 900 jin per mu, maize a bit more, maybe 1100 jin in a good year. I do not expect miracles, I just do not want a bad year.
